projects.name: Ado Fan Hub (In Development)
projects.description: Developing a free, unofficial, mobile-first fan companion for iOS, Android, and Web. The project is in early development; news aggregation, notifications, merchandise tracking, and multilingual interfaces are planned features, not a launched service.
highlights: Initialized an Expo mobile application and verified its Web development environment
Planning official news updates, concert reminders, merchandise release and restock tracking, and personalized notifications
Planning Japanese, English, and Traditional Chinese interfaces with region and time zone preferences
FastAPI and PostgreSQL or Supabase are planned backend options; mobile device testing and a public beta remain on the roadmap

projects.name: Audio-Visual Reasoning for Video Understanding
projects.description: An ongoing NYU Computer Vision research project investigating how multimodal models combine visual and auditory evidence, especially when sound sources are off-screen or occluded and temporal alignment is essential. Benchmarking and improvement methods are planned; no completed results are claimed.
highlights: Planning error analysis of visual shortcuts, hallucinations, unseen sound sources, and audio-visual temporal relationships
Planning comparisons of audio-plus-video, video-only, audio-only, and mismatched or time-shifted audio conditions
Planning a curated or synthesized evaluation set organized by identified failure cases
Exploring training-free alignment and evidence reconciliation, alongside potential LoRA fine-tuning and representation analysis

projects.name: LLM-Based CUDA Configuration Optimizer (In Progress)
projects.description: An NYU GPUs: Architecture and Programming team project investigating whether LLMs can recommend effective CUDA grid and block launch configurations. The work is in progress; experimental results have not yet been reported in the project README.
highlights: Planning an automated workflow comparing LLM launch recommendations with empirical configuration sweeps
Targeting at least 20 CUDA benchmark programs across multiple problem sizes; this is the planned evaluation scope
Studying how kernel code, problem size, GPU specifications, and prompt detail affect recommendations
Planning runtime and performance-gap analysis using the NYU CIMS CUDA computing environment

projects.name: AI Secure Software Advisor
projects.description: Built a local MVP for scanning pinned Python dependencies for known vulnerabilities and proposing upgrade candidates checked against OSV, PyPI metadata, and target Python and wheel compatibility. Optional AI explanations summarize structured scan evidence.
highlights: Implemented batch vulnerability scans with CVE/GHSA/PYSEC alias deduplication and CVSS severity evidence
Verified upgrade candidates against package release metadata, target wheel tags, and a second OSV query
Added optional direct dependency checks, downloadable upgrade drafts, and a five-language web interface
Integrated optional local Ollama or cloud OpenAI explanations; the scanner works independently of AI

projects.name: AI-Powered Personal Portfolio Assistant
projects.description: Built an AI portfolio assistant that answers resume-grounded questions with source navigation. The current cloud deployment uses a server-side Next.js API route on Vercel with Gemini; the original prototype used FastAPI and Ollama.
highlights: Built a responsive Next.js portfolio with an integrated AI chat interface
Migrated AI inference from a local FastAPI/Ollama prototype to the Gemini cloud API on Vercel
Implemented resume-grounded responses with validated portfolio source references
Kept API credentials server-side and added request limits, timeouts, and clear error handling

projects.name: Subway Congestion Decision Support Platform
projects.description: Built an NYU-area subway congestion decision support application using historical MTA ridership data.
highlights: Loaded and validated hourly MTA ridership observations in PostgreSQL
Used a persisted Random Forest model for congestion prediction
Generated commuter recommendations based on predictions
Stored predictions, recommendations, and user decisions in PostgreSQL

projects.name: Cloud-Based Intelligent Taekwondo Motion Classification System
projects.description: Built an end-to-end AI system that analyzes taekwondo videos using pose estimation and machine learning.
highlights: Built video preprocessing, pose extraction, feature engineering, model training, and inference workflows
Trained a Random Forest classifier on more than 400 labeled motion samples
Classified five taekwondo kick categories
Achieved more than 90 percent cross-validation accuracy
Deployed a Streamlit inference application on AWS EC2
Integrated AWS S3 and Oracle Object Storage

projects.name: Promotions Microservice with CI/CD Deployment Pipeline
projects.description: Developed a RESTful promotions management microservice and contributed to automated testing and deployment workflows.
highlights: Implemented REST API endpoints and service actions
Added Swagger and OpenAPI documentation
Implemented automated unit and BDD testing
Worked on Tekton CI/CD pipelines
Deployed and tested the application using OpenShift and Kubernetes
Project test coverage reached approximately 98 percent

projects.name: IMDb & YouTube Movie Trailer Analytics
projects.description: Built a big data analytics pipeline that processed IMDb and YouTube trailer datasets to analyze ratings, sentiment, and movie-related trends.
highlights: Processed large-scale movie datasets using distributed systems
Built analytics workflows using Hive and Trino
Used Python and SQL for data processing and analysis

projects.name: NSTC Undergraduate Research Project
projects.description: Built a computer vision research system that transformed taekwondo videos into measurable athlete performance metrics.
highlights: Selected as an NSTC undergraduate research project
Analyzed athlete stability, consistency, and explosiveness from videos
Combined pose estimation with athlete performance analytics

projects.name: Human Activity Recognition Using CNN and Sensor Data
projects.description: Developed a CNN-based human activity recognition system using motion sensor data.
highlights: Processed multi-subject sensor data using overlapping windows
Evaluated classification performance using confusion matrices and validation metrics
Improved classification accuracy from approximately 72 percent to 97 percent
